I give up. I did not write a proof, and `/work/fatex_045.lean` still contains its original `sorry`.

I looked for a shortcut in the hypotheses and found none. They are consistent, and the grading condition is a real one. So the theorem is the graded Hilbert syzygy theorem in full. Modules over a polynomial ring in `r` variables have projective dimension at most `r`. Over an ℕ-graded ring, graded projective modules are free.

I searched the compiled Mathlib files for anything that would supply either step. I found no Hilbert syzygy theorem, global dimension for polynomial rings, Koszul complexes or Quillen–Suslin. I would have to build all of that from scratch, and that is far more than a single proof in this file can reasonably hold.
